# cato_dns_forwarding_rule (Resource)

Manages one standalone DNS forwarding rule via networkConfig.dns. Unrelated collection items remain unchanged. Requires NCS_DNS_PUBLIC_API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
// forward a single domain
resource "cato_dns_forwarding_rule" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
  server = [
    "192.0.2.53",
  ]
}

# cato_dns_forwarding_rule.kitchen_sink:
# domain and server are plain literals with no id/name reference to another tenant
# object, so a single maximal instance (6 servers, the schema's upper bound) is the
# complete kitchen sink - no by-name/by-id duality applies to this type.
resource "cato_dns_forwarding_rule" "kitchen_sink" {
  domain = "kitchensink.example.com"
  server = [
    "203.0.113.53",
    "203.0.113.54",
    "203.0.113.55",
    "203.0.113.56",
    "203.0.113.57",
    "203.0.113.58",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Unique DNS forwarding domain.
- `server` (List of String) Ordered forwarding server addresses (1–6).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Collection item IDs are opaque and must be preserved unchanged.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cato_dns_forwarding_rule.example OPAQUE_RESOURCE_ID
```
